 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/FIRST APPEAL NO. 4258 of 2024  ================================================================

 NISHIT A BHALODI(9597) for the Appellant(s) No. 1,2,3,4,5  M A HUSSENI(10096) for the Defendant(s) No. 1  MR CHIRAYU A MEHTA(3256) for the Defendant(s) No. 2  MR PRATIK G ADVANI(10574) for the Defendant(s) No. 1  ================================================================

ORAL ORDER 1. Heard learned advocate Mr. Nishit A. Bhalodi for the appellants, learned advocate Mr. M. A.
Husseni for respondent No.1 and learned advocate Mr. Chirayu Mehta for respondent No.2 at length.
Perused the record.

2. The brief facts of the case are as under:
* On 21.3.2014, the deceased Bhupatbhai was walking towards Shivshakti Hotel at about 18.30. hours.

Opponent No.1 at that time came on his motor NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4258/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined cycle bearing registration No.GJ-11-AM-5708 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed with the deceased.
The deceased sustained serious injuries and was admitted to Una Government Hospital and, thereafter, he was transferred to Junagadh Civil Hospital.
However, because of external injuries, the deceased expired.

sentences.text: 1 * FIR was registered against the driver of the motorcycle at Una Police Station.
The claimants filed a claim petition being MACP No.606 of 2017 before the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.) at Keshod for a compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.) at Keshod
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
*
Summons and notice of claim petition were issued and served upon opponents.
Opponent No.1 appeared and filed Written Statement at Exh.21.
Opponent No.2 - insurance company of the offending vehicle appeared and filed Written Statement at Exh.33 and denied its liability.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4258/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined *
Claimant No.1 filed examination in chief at Exh.38 and produced documentary evidence in support of the claim petition such as FIR, Panchnama, Charge-sheet etc.

After considering the oral evidence as well as submissions canvassed by the learned advocates for the respective parties, learned Tribunal though found that the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.11,50,000/-, granted compensation of RS.5,00,000/- by observing that the claim petition is filed for a compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- only.
The learned Tribunal awarded interest @ 8% p.a. with proportionate cost against the opponents from the date of petition till realisation to be recovered from the opponents.
* Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award of compensation, the appellants - original claimants have filed the present appeal for enhancement of compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4258/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined 3.

Learned advocate for the appellant submitted that deceased was aged about 35 years at the relevant point of time and was earning Rs.7,000/- per month by doing labour work and taking contract from the same.
However, in absence of any evidence, learned Tribunal has considered Rs.5,000/- per month as the income of the deceased.

It is further submitted that the learned Tribunal has, after considering the income and prospective income and other conventional heads,
observed that compensation comes to Rs.11,50,000/-, however, since the claimants have claimed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-, the learned Tribunal did not grant compensation more than the amount which is claimed by claimants.
4. Learned advocate for the appellant has relied upon the case of Nagappa v. Gurudayal Singh (Supra), reported in 2003(2) SCC 274, and pressed into NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4258/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined service paragraph No.21.
5.
It is submitted that under the M.V. Act, there is no restriction that compensation would be awarded only upto the amount claimed by the claimants.

In appropriate cases, where from the evidence brought on record, if the learned Tribunal considers that the claimant entitled to get more compensation than claimed, learned Tribunal has jurisdiction to pass such award in favour of the claimants.
Except the above submissions, no other submissions are canvassed by the learned advocate for the appellants.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned advocates appearing for the respondents have supported the judgment and award and submitted that learned Tribunal has rightly considered the evidence on record and awarded just and reasonable compensation.

It is submitted that when the claimants have claimed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-, learned Tribunal has granted the entire NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4258/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined amount which was claimed.
It is also submitted that merely because claimants are entitled to more amount of compensation, learned Tribunal cannot award more than the amount claimed under the claim petition.

7. Having considered the contentions and averments made in the appeal as well as submissions made by the learned advocates for the respective parties and materials placed on record, while considering the income of deceased, learned Tribunal has ignored the date of accident which is dated 21.3.2014.
On the date of accident, the prevailing rates of minimum wages was Rs.5,600/- for semi skilled workers.
The deceased being engaged in the labour work, the minimum wages would be applicable @ Rs.5,600/- per month.
So far as the question of granting of more amount of compensation than claimed, the issue is no more res integra in the decision of Nagappa (Supra).

The relevant portion of the said decision is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4258/2024 ORDER DATED:
11/03/2025 undefined reproduced hereunder:
"21.
For the reasons discussed above, in our view, under the M.V. Act, there is no restriction that Tribunal / Court cannot award compensation amount exceeding the claimed amount.
The function of the Tribunal/Court is to award 'Just' compensation which is reasonable on the basis of evidence produced on record.
Further, in such cases there is no question of claim becoming time barred or it cannot be contended that by enhancing the claim there would be change of cause of action.

It is also to be stated that as provided under sub-section (4) to Section 166, even report submitted to the Claims Tribunal under sub-section (6) of Section 158 can be treated as an application for compensation under the M.V. Act.

If required, in appropriate cases,
Court may permit amendment to the Claim Petition."

8. While discussing on the issue, Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that a function of the Tribunal /
Court is to award just compensation which is reasonable on the basis of evidence produced on record.

In the present case, when the claimants have established by way of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4258/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined evidence that they are entitled to more amount of compensation than claimed in the claim petition, the learned Tribunal would not have restricted to award compensation as claimed in the claim petition only but can award more compensation than claimed in the petition.

9. Looking to the age of deceased at the time of accident and considering the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, percentage of prospective income would be 40% instead of 50%.

Therefore, total amount of compensation would come to Rs.14,07,260/-, which is required to be awarded with 8% p.a. interest from date of claim petition till its realisation, which would meet the ends of justice.

It is pertinent to note that learned Tribunal has already awarded Rs.5,00,000/- to the claimant, therefore, Rs.9,07,260/- (Rs.14,07,260- Rs.5,00,000/-) is required to be enhanced with interest @ 7% p.a..

12 . It is clarified that at the time of condonation of delay in preferring appeal, it was directed by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4258/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 21.11.2024 that claimants shall not be entitled to receive interest on enhanced amount for the period 730 days in case of applicants would be entitled to get enhanced compensation.

Keeping in mind, the claimants are not entitled to interest for the delayed period i.e.
of 730 days on enhanced amount.
The Insurance company shall calculate the amount accordingly.
Once the enhanced amount is deposited by the Insurance Company, the learned Tribunal shall disburse the same in favour of the claimants as per law procedure.
13. For the reasons recorded hereinabove, the following order is passed:
[A]. The present appeal is partly allowed accordingly in above terms.

[B]. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount Rs.9,07,260/- with 7% p.a. interest from the date of claim petition NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4258/2024 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined till its realisation before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
